title: How to Build a Longevity Hedge Into Your Retirement Plan
description: Preparing for the financial risk of living to 100.
content:
Living a long life is a goal, but financially, it is a risk. 'Longevity Risk' is the danger that you outlive your savings. A retirement plan that works perfectly until age 85 is a failure if you live to 95. As medical technology advances, planning for a 30-40 year retirement is becoming standard. You cannot rely on a conservative bond portfolio for 40 years; inflation will eat it alive. You need a specific 'Longevity Hedge'—assets that kick in or keep growing late in life.

Key Takeaways

  • Deferred Annuities (QLAC): A Qualified Longevity Annuity Contract allows you to use IRA money today to buy a guaranteed income stream that starts at age 80 or 85. It is 'Old Age Insurance'.
  • Delay Social Security: Claiming at 70 is the best longevity hedge. It maximizes the inflation-adjusted government check that lasts as long as you do.
  • Rising Equity Glidepath: Counter-intuitively, some research suggests increasing your stock allocation in your 70s and 80s to fight the compounding effects of inflation over a super-long life.
  • Home Equity Reserve: Your home is the asset of last resort. A Reverse Mortgage (HECM) line of credit can be tapped at age 90 if liquid assets run dry.

Why It Matters (US Context)

For a married couple age 65, there is a 50% chance one spouse lives to 92 and a 25% chance one lives to 97. Betting on dying at 85 is betting against the odds.

The Centenarian Portfolio

How to fund the years 85-100.

1. The QLAC Layer

Strategy: Take $100,000 from your IRA at age 65. Buy a QLAC.
Payout: Pays $0 for 20 years. Starts paying ~$2,500/mo at age 85 for life.
Benefit: You now have permission to spend your other assets down to zero by age 85, because the QLAC refuels the tank then.

2. The Social Security Layer

Delaying to 70 creates a larger base.
Since COLA (Cost of Living Adjustment) is a percentage, a larger base compound faster. In your 90s, a delayed benefit might be double an early benefit.

3. The Growth Layer

You cannot hold 100% bonds. Inflation of 3% cuts purchasing power in half every 24 years.
Action: Maintain 40-50% in stocks forever. You need the growth to pay the bills in 2050.

Tactical Adjustments

  1. Variable Withdrawals: Be willing to spend less in down markets. This preserves the principal so it can last 40 years.
  2. Healthspan Investment: The most expensive part of old age is being sick. Investing in fitness now reduces the 'Nursing Home' risk later.
  3. Long Term Care Insurance: Living to 100 increases the probability of cognitive decline. A policy ensures you can pay for memory care without bankrupting the surviving spouse.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is a QLAC safe?

Yes, up to state guaranty limits (usually $250k). Buy from top-rated insurers. It sits inside your IRA and reduces RMDs.

What if I die at 80?

Then the QLAC money is gone (unless you bought a death benefit rider, which lowers the payout). You 'lost' the bet, but you bought peace of mind.

Should I keep my house?

Yes. A paid-off house reduces your cash flow needs. It acts as a longevity hedge because it eliminates rent inflation.
